catholic-encyclopedia-1913-heiligenkreuz:
Austria's Cistercian abbey of Heiligenkreuz, eight miles north-west of Baden in the Vienna woods, Margrave St. Leopold founded it in 1135 at his son Otto's request, with monks from Morimond under Abbot Gottschalk. Richly endowed by the Babenberg dukes, it survived epidemics, floods, fires, and the Turkish wars of 1529 and 1683, and nearly every abbot won note for piety and learning.

Its church joins a Romanesque nave and transept, dedicated in 1187, to a Gothic choir of the thirteenth century whose windows rank among medieval art's finest remnants. Daughter houses spread from Zwettl in 1138 to Neuberg in 1327, and today the abbey holds 50,000 volumes, its own seminary and college, and 52 priests serving 22 parishes.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ramon-de-la-c:
Ramón de la Cruz, poet, was born at Madrid, Spain, on 28 March 1731 and died in Madrid on 4 November 1795. This encyclopedia entry notes that he worked as a clerk in the Ministry of Finance, and belonged to the Royal Academy of Seville and the Arcadians of Rome. He wrote more than three hundred pieces for the stage, many of them improvised.

His habit was to sit on a stone bench in the Prado, work out a theme suggested by the scene before him, and write it up the next day. Each improvisation reached the stage within two or three days of writing. La Casa de Tócame Roque, written this way, won favour and stayed a favourite long after. At first he tried tragedies, zarzuelas and comedies, but he is best remembered as the inventor of a new short dramatic form, the sainete.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-vera-cruz:
Vera Cruz, or Jalapa, is a Mexican diocese covering almost all the state of Vera Cruz, with over 1. 1 million people at the 1910 census. Its bishop resides at Jalapa, 4,335 feet above sea level, a city of about 24,800 inhabitants.

The entry roots the diocese in Cortés's landing at Vera Cruz on Good Friday 1519. Gave the town its name, True Cross, accompanied by priests including Bartolomé de Olmedo and the interpreter Gerónimo de Aguilar, long a prisoner among the Indians. By 1524 parishes with rectors, sextons, and furnishings already existed there, and within a century the colony's importance and the faith's progress made a bishopric seem advisable.
